# nonFunction

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a function.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonFunction() — Checks whether a value is **not** a function. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonFunction<T>(value: T): value is Exclude<T, Function>;
```

`nonFunction(value)` is the same test as `!isFunction(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Classified by its internal tag, so ordinary, `async`, generator and async-generator functions all pass. A class is a function too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description         |
| :-------- | :--- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T`  | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a function; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `Exclude<T, Function>` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonFunction(null); // => true
nonFunction("fn"); // => true
nonFunction({}); // => true
nonFunction(function () {}); // => false
nonFunction(async function () {}); // => false
nonFunction(Math.max); // => false
```
